key_insight: A structure-aware encoding reduction can dramatically cut qubit usage for routing optimization without changing the underlying problem.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum hardware, lowering qubit count and circuit complexity can make logistics and routing workloads more feasible and improve solution reliability.
method: Reformulate the routing problem with fewer qubits using problem structure.
Preserve the original optimization objective while reducing encoding overhead.
Compile and run the reduced model on trapped-ion hardware.
evidence_signal: On the same trapped-ion quantum computer, the reduced formulation achieved a 100× improvement in success probability while also lowering qubit count and circuit complexity.
watch_item: The approach appears problem-structure dependent, so gains may not transfer directly to routing or optimization tasks without similar exploitable structure.
paper_title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
